name: The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong
insider_take: Sky-high luxury meets Eastern elegance at the world's highest hotel - literally occupying floors 103-118 of the International Commerce Centre.
whats_special: This architectural marvel holds the Guinness World Record as the world's highest hotel, with guest rooms starting at 1,608 feet above sea level. The infinity pool on the 118th floor offers unparalleled 360-degree views of Victoria Harbour and the city skyline. The hotel's signature restaurant, Tin Lung Heen, is the world's highest Michelin two-star Chinese restaurant.
pro_tip: Book a harbor-view room on floors 112-116 for the most spectacular vantage point of the Symphony of Lights show, and visit the Ozone bar during sunset for cocktails literally above the clouds.
dont_miss: The ESPA spa on the 116th floor for treatments with sky-high city views, afternoon tea at the Lounge & Bar with panoramic harbor vistas, and the nearby Sky100 observation deck just floors below for comparison shots of your lofty accommodation.
pros: World's highest hotel with breathtaking harbor and city views
Legendary Ritz-Carlton service and hospitality excellence
Prime Central location with easy access to shopping and business districts
Luxurious amenities including world-class spa and fine dining restaurants
cons: High-floor location may cause elevator wait times during peak hours
